title: The component-site projection for an affine scheme
statement:
Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and put $P=\pi_0(|T|)$, the quotient by connected components with its quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $P_{\mathrm{proet}}$ be the site of profinite spaces over $P$ with finite jointly surjective covering families. For a profinite map $E\to P$, there is an affine ind-etale $T$-scheme $T_E$, whose underlying locally ringed space is $|T|\times_P E$ with the inverse-image structure sheaf from $T$. Its component space is canonically $E$. The functor $E\mapsto T_E$ preserves finite limits and coverings and defines a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]
$$\pi_T:\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sh}(P_{\mathrm{proet}}).$$
For every sheaf of sets $F$ on $P_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and every quasi-compact quasi-separated object $W\to T$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ satisfying the following split-cover condition, there is a canonical identification. The condition is: for every finite pro-etale covering family $\{W_i\to W\}$ with all $W_i$ quasi-compact quasi-separated, the canonical map $p:\coprod_i W_i\to W$ has a section $\sigma:W\to\coprod_iW_i$ over $T$, with $p\sigma=\operatorname{id}_W$. The identification is
$$(\pi_T^{-1}F)(W)=F(\pi_0(|W|)\to P),$$
natural in $F$ and in maps between objects $W$ satisfying this condition. The same formula applies to sheaves of abelian groups and rings, preserving their operations.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8 and its more precise statement (affine component pullback), paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2.13 and Lemma 4.2.13(1); extension to algebraic objects by their finite-product operations.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $q:|T|\to P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] and [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite], $P$ is profinite. For a profinite $E$ put $D=\operatorname{LC}(E,A)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}D=E\times|T|$, with the structure map to $T$ given by projection. Each locally constant function has finite image on the compact space $E$ and factors through its finite clopen partition into fibres. Two such presentations agree on their common refinement. Thus $D$ is the filtered colimit of the finite products $A^{E_i}$. These are finite products of the principal localization $A_1$, so $A\to D$ is ind-Zariski and ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8; absolute locally constant algebra construction (also Stacks Tag 097D, proetale.tex, lemma-construct-profinite)

proof.text: The map $E\times|T|\to E\times P$, $(e,t)\mapsto(e,q(t))$, is a quotient map: it is a continuous surjection from a quasi-compact space to a Hausdorff space and is closed, since each closed subset of its source is quasi-compact. Its fibres are the connected components of $|T|$. Conversely a connected subset has constant image in each of the totally disconnected spaces $E$ and $P$, so these fibres are exactly the connected components of $E\times|T|$. Consequently $\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}D)=E\times P$. For $f:E\to P$, its graph $G=\{(e,f(e)):e\in E\}$ is closed. Put $Z=\{(e,t):q(t)=f(e)\}$, the inverse image of $G$. It is a closed union of components of $\operatorname{Spec}D$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8, more precise statement: the component fibre product

proof.text: Let $M$ be the multiplicative set of idempotents $a\in D$ such that $Z\subseteq D(a)$, and define the actual algebra $B=M^{-1}D$ and $T_E=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Products stay in $M$, and $1\in M$; if $Z=\varnothing$, $0\in M$ and $B=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] and [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis], the intersection of these clopen neighbourhoods is exactly $Z$: a point outside $Z$ maps outside the closed subset $G$ of the profinite space $E\times P$, so a clopen containing $G$ excludes it. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a homeomorphism onto precisely this intersection. The localization $B$ is the filtered colimit of $D_a$, $a\in M$, since finitely many denominators combine by multiplication. Therefore $D\to B$ is ind-Zariski and ind-etale; [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] makes $A\to B$ ind-etale. This constructs the required affine object without choosing unspecified existence data.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8; Stacks Tags 097C (proetale.tex, lemma-construct) and 097D (lemma-construct-profinite), with the idempotent localization written out

proof.text: At a point $(e,\mathfrak p)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}D$, evaluation identifies $D_{(e,\mathfrak p)}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Indeed every locally constant function is constant on a clopen neighbourhood of $e$; its characteristic idempotent is outside the prime and hence becomes $1$ in this local ring. Thus every fraction is the fraction of its two values at $e$; conversely constant functions define the inverse homomorphism. Further localization by $M$ leaves these local rings unchanged at points of $Z$, by the fraction formulas of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Hence the structure morphism induces isomorphisms on all stalks of the inverse-image structure sheaf from $T$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks] to the underlying sheaves identifies this structure sheaf with $\mathcal O_{T_E}$; the inverse maps preserve ring operations because the original maps do. The ringed space is therefore exactly $|T|\times_P E$ with the inverse-image sheaf specified in the statement.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8, more precise statement: pullback of the structure sheaf

proof.text: The projection $|T_E|\to E$ is surjective and has connected fibres $q^{-1}(f(e))$. A connected subset has constant image in $E$, so these fibres are exactly the connected components. The space $|T_E|$ is quasi-compact, and its projection to the Hausdorff space $E$ is closed (closed subsets are quasi-compact). It is therefore a quotient map and induces the canonical homeomorphism $\pi_0(|T_E|)\cong E$. For any scheme $W\to T$, a continuous lift $|W|\to |T|\times_P E$ over $|T|$ gives a unique scheme map $W\to T_E$: pull back the given structure-sheaf map of $W\to T$ through the identified inverse-image sheaf. It is local on stalks because the stalks on the target are those of $T$. Conversely every scheme map gives that lift. If $W$ is qcqs, such lifts are precisely continuous $P$-maps $\pi_0(|W|)\to E$, by the quotient topology and total disconnectedness of $E$. This proves the mapping bijection, including its naturality by composition.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8, fully faithful right adjoint in the more precise statement

proof.text: A continuous $P$-map $E\to E'$ now gives the unique $T$-map $T_E\to T_{E'}$ inducing it; uniqueness gives identities and composition. The same mapping description proves preservation of finite limits: maps from any scheme $W\to T$ into a finite limiting cone correspond to continuous lifts into the corresponding finite limit of profinite spaces over $P$, hence to one unique map to its $T_E$. In particular $T_P=T$ and $T_{E_1\times_E E_2}=T_{E_1}\times_{T_E}T_{E_2}$. For a finite jointly surjective family $E_i\to E$, every point $(t,e)$ lifts to some $(t,e_i)$. Each induced arrow is ind-etale by the last algebra-map clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], since both algebras are ind-etale over $A$. It is weakly etale by that node. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], these arrows between affine schemes are affine: over every affine open of the target, their inverse images are affine. They remain jointly surjective over that open. Since the family is finite, these inverse images give exactly the finite affine source opens required by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. This proves preservation of coverings, also when all spaces are empty.

source.place: Paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2.13: limit preservation and respect for coverings

proof.text: Take the small skeletons and the larger sheaf-value universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The category of profinite spaces over $P$ has finite limits: they are the usual finite products and closed equalizer subspaces in compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces, with terminal object $P\to P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] to $u:E\mapsto T_E$, using step 6. This gives the geometric morphism $\pi_T$, whose inverse image is presheaf left Kan extension followed by sheafification, and whose direct image is restriction along $u^{op}$. This invocation supplies both the adjunction and left exactness; neither is inferred just from a pointwise formula.

source.place: Paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2.13; generic site construction: Stacks Tag 00X6, sites.tex, proposition-get-morphism

proof.text: Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathbf{Prof}/P$ and $W\to T$ be qcqs. In the Kan formula of [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact], the index category before taking the opposite consists of pairs $(E,W\to T_E)$. Step 5 gives its initial object $(\pi_0(|W|)\to P,W\to T_{\pi_0(|W|)})$: the unique arrow to $(E,a)$ is the component map corresponding to $a$. Its opposite is terminal. The colimit is therefore $F(\pi_0(|W|)\to P)$: every element represented in $F(E)$ maps there by that unique arrow, and the universal cocone equations force precisely these maps. Composition on $W$ and maps of $F$ preserve the component factorizations, so this identification is natural in both variables. This computes the presheaf inverse image on all qcqs objects, before sheafification.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1), proof, first two sentences: canonical component factorization

proof.text: Let $K$ be the presheaf Kan inverse image of step 8 and $\eta:K\to K^\#$ its sheafification unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], finite disjoint unions of qcqs objects are qcqs. Connected components commute with finite disjoint unions, directly from their quotient topology. For such a union $V=\coprod_i V_i$, step 8 and the sheaf axiom of $F$ for the clopen summand cover give $K(V)=F(\coprod_i\pi_0(V_i)\to P)=\prod_i K(V_i)$, by the restriction maps. The same geometry node states $K^\#(V)=\prod_i K^\#(V_i)$ for the sheaf $K^\#$. These identifications commute with $\eta$ by its naturality. This includes the empty family: both presheaves have singleton value on the empty scheme.

source.place: Section 00W1, sheafification; finite-product reduction for the corrected split-cover evaluation

proof.text: Every covering of a qcqs $W$ has a finite affine refinement. Namely take a finite affine open cover of $W$; on each affine target open the covering condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] provides finitely many affine source opens mapping into it and covering it. Their composites give the required refinement, and their sources are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. Hence every covering used to test local equality or local representability of sections at $W$ can be replaced by a finite qcqs covering $\{W_i\to W\}$. By the hypothesis in the corrected statement, $p:V=\coprod_iW_i\to W$ then has a section $\sigma$. This hypothesis is imposed only here, after the general construction and Kan calculation; it is not asserted for arbitrary qcqs schemes.

source.place: Lemma 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), choosing a finite affine refinement

proof.text: Suppose $a,b\in K(W)$ have the same image under $\eta_W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], they agree after a covering of $W$. Refine as in step 10 to a finite qcqs covering and write $p:V\to W$, $p\sigma=\operatorname{id}_W$. Their pullbacks agree on each summand, so step 9 gives $p^*a=p^*b$ in $K(V)$. Pulling back by $\sigma$ gives $a=\sigma^*p^*a=\sigma^*p^*b=b$. Thus $\eta_W$ is injective. This uses injectivity of the finite-product restriction of $K$; it does not assume that $K$ is already separated on arbitrary objects.

source.place: Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus) and Lemma 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), local equality for the sheafification unit

proof.text: Given $t\in K^\#(W)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] supplies a cover and local lifts. Refine it by step 10 to finite qcqs $W_i$, with lifts $a_i\in K(W_i)$ and split $p:V=\coprod_iW_i\to W$. By step 9 there is a unique $a\in K(V)$ restricting to all $a_i$. The two sections $\eta_V(a)$ and $p^*t$ of $K^\#(V)$ have the same restrictions on every summand; the sheaf product formula in step 9 implies their equality. Consequently $\eta_W(\sigma^*a)=\sigma^*\eta_V(a)=\sigma^*p^*t=t$. Thus $\eta_W$ is bijective. By step 7, $K^\#=\pi_T^{-1}F$; compose $\eta_W^{-1}$ with step 8 to obtain the asserted formula. Naturality follows from that of $\eta$ and step 8, for maps between eligible objects. The section $\sigma$ proves bijectivity only and does not enter this canonical identification.

source.place: Lemma 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), local representability, followed by the explicit split-cover argument

proof.text: For an abelian-group or ring sheaf, use [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects] to regard its operations as maps out of finite powers of its underlying sheaf of sets. The inverse image preserves these powers by step 7. Naturality of the set-valued identification in step 12, applied to addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one, identifies the induced operations with those on $F(\pi_0(|W|)\to P)$. For example the addition square identifies the two maps from $F(\pi_0(|W|))^2$ with the given addition on $F(\pi_0(|W|))$; the nullary maps similarly give zero and one. The equations for the operations are preserved functorially. Thus the canonical identification is one of abelian groups or rings, and is natural in their sheaves and in eligible $W$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1), extended by finite-product operations; Stacks Section 00YR, sites.tex, section-sheaves-algebraic-structures

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-54496f9c6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 13 steps, the statement of every cited node, both citers, and Bhatt–Scholze 4.2.12–4.2.13 with the paragraph and proof around them. The coord/returns/NR.md file is not in the snapshot, so I rebuilt the counterexample myself. The old clause (BS 4.2.13(1) for all qcqs U) is false.
